core_obligations: Represent the two section functors: for the open immersions j : U -> X and j' : U' -> X, use Sheaves, Section on open immersions and the adjointness of extension by zero to see that Hom_{O_X}(j_! O_U, F) = Hom_{O_U}(O_U, F|_U) = F(U), and similarly that j'_! O_{U'} represents F -> F(U') (proof lines 727-742).

Identify the map: the obvious canonical map of O_X-modules j'_! O_{U'} -> j_! O_U corresponds under Yoneda to the restriction map F(U) -> F(U'), and the description of the stalks of the two sheaves shows that this map is injective (proof lines 743-753).

Conclude by injectivity: since I is an injective O_X-module, the induced map Hom_{O_X}(j_! O_U, I) -> Hom_{O_X}(j'_! O_{U'}, I) is surjective, which by the two identifications is exactly the surjectivity of the restriction map I(U) -> I(U') asserted by the slogan 'injectives are flasque' (proof lines 754-763).
proof_roadmap: Show that extension by zero of the structure sheaf represents the functor of sections over the open, for U and for U' (proof lines 727-742).
Using Yoneda, identify the canonical map j'_! O_{U'} -> j_! O_U with the restriction map on sections, and check it is injective by looking at stalks (proof lines 743-753).
Apply the injectivity criterion to turn that monomorphism into a surjection of Hom groups, which is the claimed surjectivity of the restriction map (proof lines 754-763).
difficulty_reason: The lemma, whose slogan is that injectives are flasque, says that for open subspaces U' contained in U of a ringed space and an injective O_X-module I, the restriction map I(U) -> I(U') is surjective (statement lines 716-723). The proof is a three-step translation of the section functor into a representable functor: extension by zero of the structure sheaf represents F -> F(U) and F -> F(U'), Yoneda turns the canonical map between the two representing sheaves into the restriction map, injectivity of that canonical map is read off on stalks, and then the injectivity criterion for injective objects converts the monomorphism into a surjection on Hom groups (proof lines 727-762). The non-formal content is exactly this change of coordinates from sections to Hom groups. The claim is H2: one coordinate change, three cited inputs.
